import os
import tempfile
import numpy as np
from mir_eval.io import load_ragged_time_series

with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', delete=False, suffix='.csv') as f:
    f.write("timestamp,f0_1,f0_2,f0_3\n")
    f.write("0.1,440.0\n")
    f.write("0.2,440.0,554.37\n")
    f.write("0.3,440.0,554.37,659.25\n")
    temp_path = f.name

try:
    times, values = load_ragged_time_series(temp_path, delimiter=',', header=True)
    
    assert isinstance(times, np.ndarray), "times should be a numpy array"
    assert isinstance(values, list), "values should be a list"
    assert len(times) == 3, "Should have 3 timestamps"
    assert len(values) == 3, "Should have 3 value arrays"
    assert np.allclose(times, [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]), "Timestamps mismatch"
    assert len(values[0]) == 1, "First row should have 1 value"
    assert len(values[1]) == 2, "Second row should have 2 values"
    assert len(values[2]) == 3, "Third row should have 3 values"
    assert np.allclose(values[2], [440.0, 554.37, 65
